title: US DOJ Charges Suspected Russian Agent for Stalking Palantir Employees in California - Slashdot
excerpt: America's Justice Department is prosecuting a suspected foreign agent in "a state-sponsored operation" that targeted tech workers in Palo Alto, California. "We will not tolerate any efforts — by foreign governments or otherwise — to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligen...
content_html:
America's Justice Department is prosecuting a suspected foreign agent in "a state-sponsored operation" that targeted tech workers in Palo Alto, California. "We will not tolerate any efforts — by foreign governments or otherwise — to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations," said U.S. Attorney Craig H. Missakian.

The alleged Russian agent was arrested in October for "stalking and harassing employees of the software and AI firm Palantir, sources told ABC News, because of its assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia." The indictment says D'iu traveled from Istanbul to Mexico City last June and was connected with a person who helped him illegally cross the southern U.S. border. Once in the U.S., he was instructed to purchase laptops, cellphones and remote access software that his co-conspirators used to help him in his alleged targeting of the company's employees. At one point, prosecutors say D'iu was directed by his co-conspirators to visit a coffee shop where many of the company's employees would work and try to identify them and take pictures of their screens while they were working...

In September, prosecutors say D'iu allegedly followed a female employee of the company in his vehicle for nearly 30 miles after she left the company's Palo Alto, California, office. Even as the employee attempted various maneuvers to evade him, D'iu aggressively sought to follow her until she ultimately phoned police and was instructed to drive to the San Francisco Police Department's Mission Station.


The nonprofit news site Palo Alto Online notes the government's affidavit "identified at least two other instances in early September in which employees of the defense company reported being followed by a car matching the description of D'iu's silver Lexus SUV. The coffee shops and other locations where D'iu stationed his laptop — sometimes for hours at a time — are in close proximity to the Palantir office in downtown Palo Alto... FBI agents executed a search warrant on Oct. 8 at D'iu's residence in East Palo Alto. There they found the California state ID, passport and Social Security card that were present in the DHL packages, as well as two Russian passports, $18,000 in cash and a notebook with 10 Palo Alto area addresses. Five of them correlate to the home addresses of employees at the unnamed Silicon Valley defense company. The agents also recovered three employee "target package profiles" that included their names, names of relatives, education and employment history, leadership qualities and a list of strengths and weaknesses.

After searching D'iu's phone, the FBI found messages from a Telegram contact with photos of four employees and their addresses. D'iu was instructed to act like a food delivery driver and knock on their doors to verify if the employees did live at those addresses, according to the affidavit...

If convicted of all charges, D'iu could face a cumulative maximum sentence of 21 years in federal prison and $850,000 in fines.
